sources.entry: IFM - Single script file manager. MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: IFM is a single-file, web-based file manager written in PHP with a browser UI for browsing, editing, uploading and archiving files on a server.
summary.what_it_does: IFM is delivered as one PHP script that serves an HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript interface. It lets you create, edit, copy, move, download and delete files and directories, and change permissions. Uploads can be made directly, by drag and drop, or remotely via a URL. It can extract tar, tgz, tar.gz, tar.bz2 and zip archives and preview images. Access can be protected with simple authentication, optionally via LDAP ldap_bind. The README also describes vim-style keybindings and an ACE-based editor.
use_cases: manage files on a web server through a browser
edit files on a remote server from a web page
upload files to a server by URL or drag and drop
extract archives on a server without shell access
run a password-protected web file manager
how_to_run: Download ifm.php (or a CDN variant) from GitHub Releases, or build from source with 'make build-all' into ./dist
Drop the chosen *.php file into a directory served by a PHP-enabled web server
Or run with Docker: docker run --rm -d --name ifm -p 8080:80 -v /path/to/data:/var/www ifm:latest (after building the image)
Or use Docker Compose: docker compose up -d (after building the image)
notable: Ships as a single PHP file, with bundled or CDN-loaded asset flavours
Remote upload via URL and archive extraction built in
Protects .htaccess from being viewed or edited by default
Version is derived from git tags at build time
caveats: The shipped docker-compose.yml uses hard-coded admin/admin inline credentials and must be changed before production use
Minified *.min.php versions are described as not recommended
Requires several PHP extensions (bz2, curl, fileinfo, ldap for LDAP, zip and others)
